title: const, let, var: which one?
why_it_matters: Picking the right keyword prevents a family of surprise bugs.
explanation: Use const by default: the name can't be pointed at a new value. Use let when you must reassign, like a counter. Avoid var, because it ignores block boundaries and leaks out of if statements and loops.
try_it: Uncomment the price line and read the error message out loud.

title: Center anything in three lines
why_it_matters: Centering is the classic CSS fight, and grid ends it.
explanation: Grid has a built-in shortcut. Make the parent a grid, then add place-items: center. The child lands in the middle both ways. The parent needs some height, otherwise there is no spare space to center inside.
try_it: Give a div a border, put a button inside it, and center the button with only these lines.

title: SELECT only the columns you need
why_it_matters: Asking for less data makes queries faster and responses smaller.
explanation: SELECT picks which columns come back, and FROM names the table. The asterisk means every column, which is fine for exploring. In real apps list the columns you actually use, especially on phones with slow connections.
try_it: Run a select on any table and list just two columns.

title: A component is just a function
why_it_matters: Once this clicks, React stops feeling like magic.
explanation: A React component is a function that returns JSX, the HTML-looking syntax. Its name starts with a capital letter. You use it like a custom tag. Return one root element, or wrap siblings in a fragment.
try_it: Create a Footer component and render it twice.

title: In the App Router, folders are routes
why_it_matters: Understanding this file structure is half of Next.js.
explanation: Inside the app folder, every folder is a URL segment. A route becomes public only when it has a page file. So app/about/page.js is the /about page. No router configuration is needed.
code:
mkdir -p app/about
touch app/about/page.js
# now /about exists
try_it: Create a /contact route and open it in the browser.

title: Read a file's name, size and type
why_it_matters: Client-side file tools all start with the file input.
explanation: An input of type file gives you a FileList in input.files. Each File has name, size in bytes and type. Always check that a file was chosen, because users can cancel the dialog and files[0] becomes undefined.
try_it: Choose a file and convert its size to kilobytes.

title: Use a real button, not a clickable div
why_it_matters: Real buttons work with keyboards and screen readers for free.
explanation: A button is focusable, activates with Enter and Space, and is announced as a button. A div with onclick does none of that unless you rebuild it by hand. Reach for the right element first.
code: Pay
try_it: Find one clickable div in your project and swap it for a button.

title: Git in three words: edit, stage, commit
why_it_matters: The mental model matters more than the commands.
explanation: You edit files in your working folder. git add moves chosen changes to the staging area. git commit saves that staged snapshot to history. Staging lets you commit related changes together instead of everything at once.
code:
git add index.html
git commit -m "Add hero section"
git log --oneline
try_it: Make a tiny change and walk through all three steps.

title: Read AI code top to bottom, out loud
why_it_matters: You can't maintain code you can't explain.
explanation: Go one line at a time and say what each does in plain words. Anything you can't explain is where bugs will hide. Ask the AI to explain only those lines. Start with imports, then inputs, then outputs.
try_it: Take one AI-written function and explain every line to yourself.

title: Before vs after: string building
why_it_matters: Template literals make messages readable and cut missing-space bugs.
explanation: Backticks let you drop values into text with ${ }. Anything inside the braces is real JavaScript, so you can do math or call functions. It beats gluing pieces together with plus signs.
try_it: Rewrite one string-with-plus in your project using backticks.

title: Quiz: justify-content or align-items?
why_it_matters: Mixing up the two flexbox alignment properties costs beginners hours.
explanation: Flexbox has a main axis and a cross axis. justify-content works along the main axis. align-items works along the cross axis. By default the main axis is horizontal, but flex-direction: column flips both of them.
try_it: Quiz: after adding flex-direction: column, which property now centers items left to right? (Answer: align-items.)

title: Internship CV: one page, projects first
why_it_matters: Recruiters give a CV seconds, so make those seconds count.
explanation: Without work experience, projects are your proof. Lead with two or three, each with what it does, the tech used and a live link. Then skills and education. One page, plain layout, no photo and no rating bars.
try_it: Rewrite one project as a single bullet: what it does and for whom.

title: WHERE: filter rows like a pro
why_it_matters: Almost every useful query has a WHERE clause.
explanation: WHERE keeps only rows that match a condition. Combine conditions with and, or. Text values go in single quotes, never double quotes. Use = for equals, since SQL uses one equals sign, not two.
code:
select title
from posts
where published = true
  and views > 100;
try_it: Write a query for posts with fewer than 10 views.

title: == vs ===: the quiet bug maker
why_it_matters: Loose equality gives odd results that are hard to spot.
explanation: === compares value and type. == quietly converts types first, so strange things become true, like 0 == false. Use === everywhere, and you only have to remember one set of rules.
code:
console.log(5 == "5");     // true (surprise)
console.log(5 === "5");    // false
console.log(0 == false);   // true
console.log(0 === false);  // false
try_it: Search your code for == and replace each one with ===.

title: Props: pass data into components
why_it_matters: Props make one component reusable everywhere.
explanation: Props are the arguments of a component, passed like HTML attributes. Destructure them in the parameter list for tidy code. Strings go in quotes. Anything else, like numbers or variables, goes inside curly braces.
try_it: Add a third prop called currency and show it.

title: layout.js wraps your pages
why_it_matters: Shared navbars and fonts live here, written once.
explanation: A layout receives children, which is the current page, and wraps it. The root layout is required and holds the html and body tags. Layouts stay mounted as you navigate, so shared UI doesn't reload.
try_it: Add a nav element above children in your root layout.

title: Read a text file in the browser
why_it_matters: No upload, no server: the data never leaves the device.
explanation: A File has a text() method that returns a promise of its contents. Use it for txt, csv, json and code files. For binary files use arrayBuffer() instead. It's the base of every in-browser viewer.
try_it: Load a JSON file and pretty-print it with JSON.stringify(obj, null, 2).

title: Before vs after: spacing with gap
why_it_matters: Less CSS means fewer spacing bugs on the last item.
explanation: The old way puts a margin on every item, then removes it from the last one. The modern way sets gap on the parent. The gap only appears between items, never on the outside edges. It works in flexbox and grid.
try_it: Find one place in your project that uses margins between siblings and swap it for gap.

title: Quiz: is an empty array truthy?
why_it_matters: Truthiness decides every if statement, so it pays to know it cold.
explanation: In an if, JavaScript turns values into true or false. The falsy ones are false, 0, empty string, null, undefined and NaN. Everything else is truthy, including empty arrays and empty objects. That surprises people.
try_it: Quiz: is the string '0' truthy or falsy? Check in the console. (Answer: truthy.)

title: Newest first with ORDER BY and LIMIT
why_it_matters: Feeds and 'latest' lists use this exact pair.
explanation: ORDER BY sorts the results, ascending by default. Add desc for biggest or newest first. LIMIT caps how many rows return. Without ORDER BY, the row order is not guaranteed, so never rely on it.
code:
select title, created_at
from posts
order by created_at desc
limit 5;
try_it: Get the 3 most expensive products from any table.

title: Every input needs a label
why_it_matters: A placeholder disappears as you type and is not a label.
explanation: A label tells screen readers what the field is for, and makes the label text tappable on a phone. Connect it with for and id. Keep it visible, since placeholders vanish once someone starts typing.
code:
<label for="email">Email</label>
<input id="email" type="email" autocomplete="email">
try_it: Tap the label text on a phone and see whether the input gets focus.

title: Before vs after: commit messages
why_it_matters: Future you will search history to find out why something changed.
explanation: Write what the commit does, in the present tense, in a short line. 'fix stuff' tells nobody anything. A good message says what changed and ideally why. You can read your whole project history in one skim.
code:
git commit -m "stuff"
git commit -m "Fix cart total rounding"
try_it: Run git log --oneline and rewrite your three worst messages in your head.

title: Spot hallucinated functions fast
why_it_matters: AI confidently invents methods that don't exist.
explanation: Red flags: a method you've never seen, an import path that looks too neat, or an error saying 'is not a function'. Search the official docs for the name, or check your editor's autocomplete. If it doesn't appear, it was made up.
code:
// [[1], [2]].flatten();  // TypeError: not a function (invented)
console.log([[1], [2]].flat()); // [1, 2] (real)
try_it: Pick one unfamiliar method from AI code and verify it in the docs.

title: Two ways to write a function
why_it_matters: You will see both styles in every codebase and AI answer.
explanation: A function declaration starts with the word function and can be called before it appears in the file. An arrow function is stored in a variable and is shorter. Arrows are popular for small callbacks, like inside map.
try_it: Turn one function you wrote into an arrow function and run it.

title: Cards that wrap themselves
why_it_matters: Wrapping rows are the base of most responsive card layouts.
explanation: flex-wrap lets items drop to the next line instead of squashing. The flex shorthand sets grow, shrink and basis. flex: 1 1 220px means: start at 220px wide, share leftover space, and shrink if needed. Cards wrap when there is no room.
try_it: Add six cards and resize the browser. Count how many fit per row at each width.

title: The children prop wraps content
why_it_matters: It is how you build cards, modals and layouts.
explanation: Anything you place between a component's opening and closing tags arrives as the children prop. That lets one Card component wrap any content. It is the same idea as a slot in other frameworks.
try_it: Use Card twice with different content inside.

title: Components are server components by default
why_it_matters: It changes where your code runs and what you can use.
explanation: In the App Router, a component without any directive runs on the server. Its console.log shows in your terminal. It can read secrets and talk to the database directly, but can't use useState, effects or browser events.
try_it: Add a console.log to a page and find where it prints.

title: Preview data with object URLs
why_it_matters: It lets you show a file without reading it into memory twice.
explanation: URL.createObjectURL makes a temporary link to a File or Blob that works inside your page. Use it as an iframe or link target. It holds memory until you call revokeObjectURL, so clean up when finished.
try_it: Open the logged URL in a new tab before revoking it.

title: Default values for parameters
why_it_matters: It saves you from undefined showing up in your output.
explanation: If someone calls a function without an argument, the parameter becomes undefined. A default value fills in a fallback automatically. It only kicks in for undefined, not for null or empty strings.
try_it: Add a default quantity of 1 to an addToCart function.

title: INSERT: add a row
why_it_matters: Creating data is the first half of CRUD.
explanation: List the columns you are filling, then the values in the same order. Columns you skip use their default or null. Strings use single quotes, and booleans are true or false.
code:
insert into todos (title, done)
values ('Learn SQL', false);
try_it: Insert two rows in one statement by adding a comma and another set of values.

title: Responsive grid with zero media queries
why_it_matters: One line gives you a layout that adapts from phone to desktop.
explanation: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(220px, 1fr)) tells the grid: make as many columns as fit, each at least 220px, and stretch them to fill the row. On a phone you get one column. On a laptop you get four. No breakpoints needed.
try_it: Change 220px to 160px and watch how many columns appear on your phone.

title: Make your GitHub profile README
why_it_matters: It is the first page a curious recruiter will open.
explanation: A repo named exactly like your username, with a README, shows on your profile. Keep it short: who you are, what you're learning, your best projects and how to contact you. Avoid pages of badges and statistics.
try_it: Write a four-line profile README today and publish it.

title: Mistake: the function that returns undefined
why_it_matters: Forgetting return is one of the most common beginner bugs.
explanation: Arrow functions with curly braces need an explicit return. Without braces, the value after the arrow is returned automatically. If a function gives you undefined, check for a missing return first.
code:
const double = (n) => { n * 2 };   // no return
const doubleOk = (n) => n * 2;     // implicit return
console.log(double(4), doubleOk(4)); // undefined 8
try_it: Write a function with braces and no return, log it, then fix it.

title: Check your text contrast
why_it_matters: Faint grey text is unreadable outdoors on a phone.
explanation: The common AA guideline asks for a contrast ratio of at least 4.5 to 1 for normal text. Light grey on white often fails. A grey like #767676 on white is about the lightest that still passes. Use DevTools to check ratios.
try_it: Inspect a grey text color in DevTools and read its contrast ratio.

title: Check before you commit
why_it_matters: It catches stray files and half-finished changes.
explanation: git status lists changed and untracked files. git diff shows exact line changes not yet staged. git diff --staged shows what will go into the next commit. Run them before every commit, like a spell check.
code:
git status
git diff
git diff --staged
try_it: Run git diff --staged before your next commit and read it all.

title: Old patterns: when AI uses outdated code
why_it_matters: The code runs on yesterday's version of your framework.
explanation: AI learned from years of old examples. It might hand you Pages Router code for an App Router project, or an old Supabase method name. Tell it your framework, version and router in the prompt. Check docs when something looks unfamiliar.
try_it: Ask AI for the same task twice, mentioning your exact setup the second time.

title: useState: a component's memory
why_it_matters: Without state, nothing on your page can change.
explanation: useState gives you a value and a function to update it. When you call the setter, React re-renders the component with the new value. Never change the variable directly. Always use the setter.
try_it: Add a second button that resets the count to 0.

title: When you need 'use client'
why_it_matters: You will hit this error many times, so know the fix.
explanation: Put 'use client' at the very top of a file when it needs state, effects, event handlers or browser APIs. Things like a file input, a click counter or localStorage all need it. Client-side tools are mostly client components.
try_it: Remove 'use client' from a component using useState and read the error.

title: Drag and drop files onto a page
why_it_matters: Dropping a file feels much nicer than the file picker.
explanation: Listen to dragover and call preventDefault, or the browser won't allow a drop. In the drop handler, call preventDefault again and read e.dataTransfer.files. Always keep a normal file input too, for keyboard and phone users.
try_it: Drop three files and log their combined size.

title: UPDATE and DELETE always need WHERE
why_it_matters: Forgetting it changes or deletes every single row.
explanation: Without WHERE, UPDATE and DELETE hit the whole table. Safer habit: write a SELECT with the same WHERE first and check the rows it returns. Then change select to update or delete.
try_it: Practice on a throwaway table, never on real data.

title: What 1fr really means
why_it_matters: The fr unit is the easiest way to mix fixed and flexible columns.
explanation: 1fr is one share of the leftover space, not a fixed size. Fixed columns take their space first. Whatever remains is split by fr values. A sidebar of 240px beside a 1fr column gives you a content area that always fills the rest.
try_it: Try 1fr 2fr instead. Predict the widths before you check them in DevTools.

title: Why does my loop print 3, 3, 3?
why_it_matters: This classic trap explains how scope really works.
explanation: var is function-scoped, so every callback shares one variable that ends at 3. let creates a fresh variable for each loop pass, so each callback keeps its own value. That is another reason to forget var.
try_it: Run both loops in the console and predict the output first.

title: Arrays: counting starts at zero
why_it_matters: Off-by-one errors start here.
explanation: The first item is at index 0, and the last is at length minus 1. .length tells you how many items there are. .at(-1) grabs the last item without math. push adds to the end and returns the new length.
try_it: Without running it, predict tabs[3] before and after the push.

title: Name your layout with grid areas
why_it_matters: Named areas make a page layout readable like a drawing.
explanation: grid-template-areas lets you draw the layout in text. Each quoted row is a row of the grid, and each word is a cell name. Then assign elements to names with grid-area. Rearranging for mobile is just rewriting the drawing.
try_it: Sketch a page with header, nav, main and footer, then write the areas for it.

title: Pick the right column types
why_it_matters: Wrong types cause rounding bugs and messy data later.
explanation: Use text for words, integer for whole numbers, boolean for true or false, and timestamptz for date and time. For money, store integer cents instead of decimals. A uuid primary key with a default creates ids for you.
code:
create table bookings (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  guest_name text not null,
  nights integer not null,
  total_cents integer not null,
  created_at timestamptz default now()
);
try_it: Sketch a table for something you build, and choose a type for each column.

title: Before vs after: updating array state
why_it_matters: Mutating state is the top reason a screen doesn't update.
explanation: React compares state by reference. If you push into the same array and set it back, React sees no change and skips the update. Create a new array with spread instead. The same applies to objects.
try_it: Write a removeItem that uses filter to return a new array.

title: Before vs after: push 'use client' down
why_it_matters: Smaller client components mean less JavaScript sent to the phone.
explanation: Marking a whole page as client makes everything inside it client code. Instead, keep the page a server component and put the interactive bit, like a like button, in its own small client file. Import it where needed.
try_it: Find a page marked 'use client' and extract only the interactive part.

title: Download a file you generated
why_it_matters: Export buttons need no backend at all.
explanation: Create a Blob from your data, make a link to it with an object URL, give it a download name and click it with code. This works for CSV exports, JSON backups and any text you generate in the page.
try_it: Export your localStorage cart as a JSON download.

title: Test your site with only a keyboard
why_it_matters: It finds more accessibility bugs than any tool in two minutes.
explanation: Put your mouse away and press Tab. Can you reach every link and button? Can you always see where you are? Does Enter or Space activate things? Does a modal let you escape and return focus? Fix whatever breaks.
try_it: Tab through your homepage and write down the first thing that breaks.

title: Set up .gitignore on day one
why_it_matters: It keeps junk and secrets out of your repository.
explanation: Files named in .gitignore are skipped by Git. Always ignore node_modules, build output like .next, and env files holding secrets. Add it before the first commit, because ignoring doesn't remove already tracked files.
code:
printf "node_modules
.next
.env.local
" >> .gitignore
try_it: Open your .gitignore and check these three lines exist.

title: Context makes prompts work
why_it_matters: Vague questions get vague code.
explanation: Include your stack, what you want, what you already tried, and what 'done' looks like. For example: Next.js App Router, Supabase, mobile layout. One clear goal per prompt beats a giant request. The more specific, the less you rewrite.
try_it: Rewrite your last vague prompt with stack, goal and constraints.

title: map: turn one array into another
why_it_matters: map powers almost every list you will render in React.
explanation: map runs a function on every item and returns a new array of the same length. The original array stays untouched. Use it when you want a transformed copy, like pulling just the names out of a list of users.
try_it: Use map to turn [1, 2, 3] into [10, 20, 30].

title: Mobile-first: start small, grow up
why_it_matters: Most of your users are on phones, so phones should get the simple CSS.
explanation: Write the phone layout as your default styles. Then use min-width media queries to add things for bigger screens. You end up with less overriding, and phones don't have to download and undo desktop rules.
try_it: Take a page you built desktop-first and move one section to this pattern.

title: Pin your best repos only
why_it_matters: Your profile should show your strongest work first.
explanation: GitHub lets you pin up to six repositories. Pick finished, readable projects with a clear README and a live demo. Hide forks and tutorial copies from the spotlight. Quality shows more than quantity here.
try_it: Choose the three projects you'd show a recruiter and pin them.

title: Let the database reject bad data
why_it_matters: Constraints protect you even when your app code has a bug.
explanation: not null forbids empty values. check enforces a rule, like nights above zero. unique stops duplicates, like two accounts with the same email. Database rules apply to every client, so they are your last line of defense.
try_it: Try to insert a booking with 0 nights and read the error.

title: filter: keep only what you need
why_it_matters: Search boxes and tabs are all filter underneath.
explanation: filter runs a test on each item and keeps the ones where your function returns true. You get a new, possibly shorter array. The test function should return true or false, not a value to transform.
try_it: Filter an array of numbers to keep only the even ones.

title: Why setCount twice only adds one
why_it_matters: State updates are scheduled, not instant.
explanation: Within one event, count holds the same value on every line, so two setCount(count + 1) calls both set it to the same number. Pass a function to the setter instead. It receives the latest value, and updates stack up.
try_it: Make a button that adds 3 in a single click using the function form.

title: Fetch data right inside the component
why_it_matters: No useEffect, no loading state: the server does the waiting.
explanation: A server component can be async. Await your data directly, and the page arrives with the content already filled in. Keep secrets like API keys in environment variables, since this code never ships to the browser.
try_it: Fetch data in a server component instead of useEffect in one page.

title: Compress images in the browser
why_it_matters: Smaller uploads save your users' data and your storage costs.
explanation: Decode the file into a bitmap, draw it on a canvas, then export with toBlob and a lower quality value. Quality only applies to JPEG and WebP. You can also shrink width and height before drawing for bigger savings.
try_it: Compare file.size with the returned blob.size for three quality values.

title: The missing viewport tag mistake
why_it_matters: Without this tag your responsive CSS looks broken on a real phone.
explanation: Mobile browsers pretend to be a wide desktop screen unless you tell them otherwise, then shrink the page down. Your media queries never fire as expected. One meta tag in the head fixes it. Put it in every project.
code: <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
try_it: Delete the tag from a test page, open it on your phone, and compare.

title: reduce: many values, one result
why_it_matters: Cart totals and counters use this pattern constantly.
explanation: reduce walks through an array while carrying an accumulator. Each step returns the new accumulator. You provide a starting value as the second argument. Sums, totals and grouping are all reduce at heart.
try_it: Write a reduce that finds the highest number in an array.

title: Foreign keys connect your tables
why_it_matters: Relational data is the whole point of SQL.
explanation: A foreign key column stores the id of a row in another table. The database then refuses ids that don't exist. Here, each payment must belong to a real booking. This is how you avoid duplicated, drifting data.
try_it: Try inserting a payment with a made-up booking_id.

title: 'Click here' is a useless link
why_it_matters: Screen reader users often jump through a list of links alone.
explanation: Link text should make sense out of context. 'Click here' or 'read more' tells nobody anything when listed. Describe the destination instead. It also helps people scanning quickly on a phone and improves search results.
code: Click here See pricing plans
try_it: Search your pages for 'click here' and rewrite each link.

title: Mistake: you committed a secret key
why_it_matters: Deleting it in a new commit doesn't remove it from history.
explanation: Anyone who can see the repo can still read old commits. Treat a leaked key as compromised: rotate or regenerate it in the provider's dashboard right away, then update your environment variables. Cleaning history is secondary to rotating.
try_it: List every key your project uses and note where each one lives.

title: Paste the exact error, with the code
why_it_matters: Paraphrasing an error removes the clue.
explanation: Copy the full error message and the few lines of code around where it points. Add what you expected to happen. Leave out unrelated files. Exact text lets the AI, and you, search for the real cause instead of guessing.
try_it: Next error you get, copy it exactly and read it before asking anyone.

title: find vs filter: one or many?
why_it_matters: Mixing them up gives you an array when you wanted an object.
explanation: find returns the first matching item, or undefined if there is none. filter returns an array of every match, which may be empty. Use find when you expect one result, like looking a user up by id.
try_it: Look up an item by id with find, then print its name.

title: Fluid headings with one clamp()
why_it_matters: Headings that scale smoothly mean fewer breakpoints to maintain.
explanation: clamp takes a minimum, a preferred value and a maximum. The preferred value usually uses vw so it grows with the screen. The browser never goes below the minimum or above the maximum, so text stays readable on every device.
try_it: Apply clamp to your h1, then drag the browser width and watch it stop at both ends.

title: Rendering lists and the key prop
why_it_matters: Missing or bad keys cause weird bugs in lists that change.
explanation: Use map to turn data into elements. Every item needs a key that is unique and stable, usually the database id. Avoid the array index when items can be reordered or deleted, because React may mix up which one is which.
try_it: Check the console for the 'unique key' warning in your latest list.

title: Dynamic routes with [slug]
why_it_matters: One file can serve thousands of pages.
explanation: Wrap a folder name in square brackets to capture that URL part. app/blog/[slug]/page.js matches /blog/anything. The value arrives in params. In recent versions params is a promise, and awaiting it works either way.
try_it: Visit three different URLs under /blog and check the heading.

title: localStorage: save data between visits
why_it_matters: It is the quickest way to make an app remember things.
explanation: localStorage keeps key and value pairs in the browser, with no expiry. Values must be strings, so use JSON.stringify to save objects and JSON.parse to read them back. It is synchronous and small, so keep it for light data.
try_it: Save your name, refresh the page, and show it back.

title: Three yes/no array helpers
why_it_matters: They replace clumsy loops with a single readable line.
explanation: includes checks if a value is in the array. some asks whether at least one item passes a test. every asks whether all of them do. Each returns a plain true or false, so they fit right inside an if.
code:
const scores = [40, 75, 90];
console.log(scores.some((s) => s > 80));   // true
console.log(scores.every((s) => s >= 50)); // false
console.log(scores.includes(75));          // true
try_it: Check whether every item in a list of prices is above zero.

title: JOIN: combine two tables
why_it_matters: Real screens need data from more than one table.
explanation: A join matches rows using a shared value, usually a foreign key. The on clause says which columns match. An inner join returns only rows that have a match on both sides. Table aliases like b and p keep it short.
try_it: List each booking beside its payment amount.

title: rem vs px: why it matters
why_it_matters: Using rem respects people who raise their default text size.
explanation: px is a fixed size. rem is relative to the root font size, which users can change in their browser settings. Sizing text and spacing in rem lets your layout grow with their preference instead of ignoring it.
try_it: Raise your browser's default font size and see which of your pages ignore it.

title: Write a README that sells the project
why_it_matters: A good README is your project's job interview.
explanation: Cover what it does, why you built it, the tech stack, how to run it locally, and a live link. Add one or two things you learned or found hard. If someone can understand your project in 30 seconds, you win.
try_it: Fix the README of your best project using this checklist.

title: Mistake: forEach is not map
why_it_matters: Expecting a result from forEach is a very common stumble.
explanation: forEach just runs a function for each item and returns undefined. If you want a new array, use map. If you only want side effects, like logging or updating the page, forEach is the right tool.
try_it: Change a forEach in your code to map if you assign its result.

title: Use landmarks instead of divs everywhere
why_it_matters: Screen reader users can jump straight to the main content.
explanation: header, nav, main and footer tell assistive tech where things are. People can skip past the navigation directly to main. Use one main per page. Semantic elements are free accessibility with no extra attributes.
code:
<header>Logo</header>
<nav>Links</nav>
<main>Page content</main>
<footer>Contact</footer>
try_it: Replace the outer divs of one page with these elements.

title: Work on branches, not main
why_it_matters: A broken experiment shouldn't break your working app.
explanation: A branch is a separate line of work. Create one for each feature, commit freely, then merge it back when ready. Branch names like feature/login describe their purpose. Main stays working, and your live site stays safe.
code: git switch -c feature/login
try_it: Create a branch for your next change instead of using main.

title: Ask for the smallest change
why_it_matters: Big rewrites hide bugs and teach you nothing.
explanation: Ask for one step at a time and a minimal change, like 'add the loading state only'. Small diffs are easy to read and test. If a reply rewrites the whole file, ask which lines actually changed and why.
try_it: Request a change and review only the diff before accepting.

title: Mistake: the 0 that appears on screen
why_it_matters: A tiny condition bug can print a stray 0 in your UI.
explanation: React renders numbers, and 0 is a number. So length && <List /> shows 0 when the array is empty. Compare explicitly with > 0, or use a ternary. Booleans, null and undefined render nothing.
try_it: Look for && with a number on the left in your code.

title: Link vs <a>: navigate without reload
why_it_matters: It makes navigation feel instant like an app.
explanation: The Link component from next/link switches pages on the client without a full reload. It can also fetch the next page's code ahead of time. Use it for internal links, and plain a tags for outside websites.
try_it: Replace one internal a tag in your project with Link.

title: Mistake: localStorage returns null
why_it_matters: JSON.parse(null) can crash a fresh visitor's first load.
explanation: A key that was never saved returns null, and everything is stored as a string. Provide a fallback before parsing. Wrap in try and catch too, because storage can be blocked or the saved text could be corrupted.
try_it: Run it after localStorage.clear() and make sure nothing crashes.

title: LEFT JOIN finds what's missing
why_it_matters: 'Which users have no orders?' is a very common question.
explanation: A left join keeps every row from the left table, even without a match. The right side's columns become null. Filtering for null on the right table gives you exactly the rows with no matches, like unpaid bookings.
code:
select b.guest_name
from bookings b
left join payments p on p.booking_id = b.id
where p.id is null;
try_it: Find users who have never posted anything.

title: Myth: 100vh fits the phone screen
why_it_matters: Full-screen hero sections often get cut off by mobile browser bars.
explanation: On phones the address bar slides away as you scroll, so 100vh is sometimes taller than the visible area. The dvh unit means dynamic viewport height and follows the real visible space. Use it for full-screen sections.
try_it: Open a full-height page on your phone, scroll a little, and see if the bottom button hides.

title: Copy an array without changing the original
why_it_matters: Mutating shared data causes bugs that appear far from their cause.
explanation: The spread operator ... unpacks an array into a new one. Use it to add or combine items without touching the original. React state updates depend on this habit.
try_it: Combine two arrays into one with spread, then log all three.

title: Dot vs bracket: reading object keys
why_it_matters: Dynamic keys and odd names need the bracket form.
explanation: Dot notation is cleanest when you know the key. Bracket notation takes any string, so it works with variables and keys that contain dashes or spaces. Use brackets when the key is stored in a variable.
try_it: Loop over ['name', 'pay-method'] and print each value using brackets.

title: One line that fixes padding overflow
why_it_matters: It stops the most common 'why is my box wider than 100%' bug.
explanation: By default, width ignores padding and border, so a width: 100% box with padding sticks out. border-box makes width include them. Most projects reset it for every element at the top of the stylesheet.
try_it: Make an input with width: 100% and padding: 20px. Toggle border-box and compare.

title: GROUP BY: totals per category
why_it_matters: Dashboards and reports are built on it.
explanation: GROUP BY collapses rows that share a value into one row. Combine it with aggregates like count, sum, avg, min and max. Every selected column must either be in the group or inside an aggregate.
code:
select booking_id,
       count(*) as payments,
       sum(amount_cents) as paid
from payments
group by booking_id;
try_it: Count how many posts each author has written.

title: Controlled inputs, explained
why_it_matters: Forms are everywhere, and this is the standard way to build them.
explanation: A controlled input gets its value from state and updates state in onChange. React is the single source of truth, so you can validate, format or clear the input at any time. Forgetting onChange makes the field read-only.
try_it: Show the typed name in a paragraph under the input.

title: Redirect users who aren't signed in
why_it_matters: Protected pages need a gate, and this is the simplest one.
explanation: Import redirect from next/navigation and call it in a server component when a check fails. The user is sent elsewhere before the page renders. Always check on the server too, not only in the browser.
try_it: Make the redirect go to /login and build a simple login page.

title: Myth: localStorage is safe for tokens
why_it_matters: A stolen login token means a stolen account.
explanation: Any script running on your page can read localStorage. If an attacker injects code, through a bad dependency or an unsafe innerHTML, they can copy what is stored there. Never put passwords or secrets in it, and prefer the session handling your auth library provides.
try_it: Open DevTools, Application tab, and look at what your sites store.

title: Name your icon-only buttons
why_it_matters: A button with only an icon is announced as just 'button'.
explanation: If a button has no visible text, give it an accessible name with aria-label. Describe the action, not the picture. Decorative symbols inside it don't need to be read out separately.
code: <button aria-label="Close dialog">✕</button>
try_it: Find every icon-only button in your app and check its name.

title: Merge a finished branch
why_it_matters: This is how your feature joins the main code.
explanation: Switch to the branch you want to update, usually main, then merge the feature branch into it. Delete the old branch when done, since the commits stay in history. Conflicts only appear when both sides changed the same lines.
code:
git switch main
git merge feature/login
git branch -d feature/login
try_it: Merge a small branch and view the result with git log --oneline.

title: Explain it back to learn it
why_it_matters: Teaching is the fastest way to find the gaps in your understanding.
explanation: After getting code, write your own explanation of how it works. Then ask the AI to point out what you got wrong. Or ask it to quiz you with three questions about the code. You'll remember more and stop copying blindly.
try_it: Explain one AI snippet in three sentences, then ask AI to grade you.

title: Destructuring: unpack in one line
why_it_matters: You will see this in every React component and API response.
explanation: Destructuring pulls properties out of an object into variables with matching names. You can set a default for missing ones, and rename with a colon. It makes functions that take objects much easier to read.
try_it: Destructure the first two items of an array: const [a, b] = ...

title: CSS variables: change a theme once
why_it_matters: Colors and sizes defined once stay consistent across the whole project.
explanation: Custom properties start with two dashes and are read with var(). Declare them on :root so everything can use them. Changing one value updates every place it is used, which makes themes and brand tweaks painless.
try_it: Move your three most repeated colors into variables.

title: Three strong projects beat ten tutorials
why_it_matters: Tutorial clones look identical to everyone else's.
explanation: Build things with your own twist and real constraints, then finish them: deploy, polish, document. Depth shows you can solve problems, not just follow steps. Choose projects that mirror what employers actually build.
try_it: Pick the project you'll finish this month and set a deadline.

title: Mistake: = null never matches
why_it_matters: Null means unknown, and unknown never equals anything.
explanation: Comparing with = null returns nothing, not even for null values. Use is null and is not null instead. This also explains why a not-equal filter can silently skip rows where the column is null.
code:
select * from profiles where avatar_url = null;   -- no rows
select * from profiles where avatar_url is null;  -- correct
try_it: Find all rows where a column is not null.

title: Update an object without mutating it
why_it_matters: It is the pattern behind every state update in React.
explanation: Spread copies an object's keys into a new one. Put your changes after the spread, and they overwrite the old values. The original object stays exactly as it was, so nothing else breaks unexpectedly.
try_it: Write a function that takes a user and returns a copy with a new name.

title: Handle a form submit
why_it_matters: Without preventDefault the page reloads and your state is gone.
explanation: Attach onSubmit to the form, not onClick to the button, so pressing Enter works too. Call preventDefault, then read values from state or from FormData. Give each input a name attribute.
try_it: Add a password field and log both values.

title: loading.js gives instant feedback
why_it_matters: Users forgive waiting when they can see something happening.
explanation: Drop a loading file in a route folder. Next.js shows it immediately while the page's async work finishes. It is the easiest way to avoid a blank screen when you fetch data on the server.
try_it: Add a 2-second delay to a page and watch your loading state.

title: IndexedDB: a database inside the browser
why_it_matters: It is where big, structured client-side data belongs.
explanation: localStorage is small and text-only. IndexedDB holds much more, supports indexes and keeps data off the main thread. You open a database with a version, and create stores inside onupgradeneeded, which runs only when the version changes.
try_it: Open DevTools, Application, IndexedDB and find your database.

title: Dark mode in six lines
why_it_matters: Many phones are set to dark mode, so a bright white page feels harsh.
explanation: The prefers-color-scheme media query reads the device setting. Define your colors as variables, then override just the variables in the dark query. Components keep using var(), so nothing else needs to change.
try_it: Switch your phone or OS to dark mode and reload your latest project.

title: Optional chaining stops crashes
why_it_matters: 'Cannot read properties of undefined' is the error you will see most.
explanation: Writing ?. means: if the thing on the left is null or undefined, stop and return undefined instead of crashing. Use it for data that may not exist yet, like API responses and optional fields.
try_it: Find a place in your code that reads two levels deep and add ?. safely.

title: Search text with ILIKE
why_it_matters: Search boxes need case-insensitive matching.
explanation: LIKE matches patterns, where % means any characters. ILIKE is the Postgres version that ignores case. A leading % can't use a normal index, so very large tables may need a better approach later.
try_it: Search your own table for names that start with 'a' (use 'a%').

title: Headings are an outline, not a font size
why_it_matters: Screen reader users navigate by headings like a table of contents.
explanation: Use one h1 for the page title, h2 for sections and h3 for subsections, without skipping levels. Choose the level for structure, then style its size with CSS. Never use a heading just because it looks bigger.
code:
Dashboard

Recent bookings

Today

Payments
try_it: Read only the headings of your page. Does it still make sense?

title: Undo changes you haven't committed
why_it_matters: Everyone breaks a file at some point.
explanation: git restore file throws away uncommitted edits in that file, permanently, so be sure. To unstage something you added by mistake, add --staged. Your edits stay in the file, but leave the next commit.
code:
git restore index.html
git restore --staged index.html
try_it: Practice both commands on a throwaway file first.

title: Rule: no code you can't explain
why_it_matters: Unexplained code becomes a trap the day something breaks.
explanation: If you can't say what a block does, don't merge it. Ask for a simpler version, or learn the concept first. This rule slows you slightly now and saves hours later. It is also exactly what interviewers probe for.
try_it: Mark the parts of your project you couldn't explain, and study one.

title: ?? vs ||: the zero bug
why_it_matters: || treats 0 and empty string as missing, which corrupts real data.
explanation: || falls back whenever the left side is falsy, including 0 and ''. ?? only falls back for null or undefined. If 0 or an empty string is a valid value, like a quantity, use ??.
try_it: Set qty to an empty string and compare both lines.

title: Keep box shapes with aspect-ratio
why_it_matters: It stops layouts from jumping around while content loads.
explanation: aspect-ratio reserves a shape for an element based on its width. A 16 / 9 box stays that shape at any size. It is great for video embeds, cards and placeholders, and replaces the old padding-top hack.
try_it: Make a square avatar placeholder with aspect-ratio: 1.

title: useEffect: run code after render
why_it_matters: It is where side effects like fetching and timers live.
explanation: useEffect runs your function after React updates the screen. The dependency array decides when it runs again: empty means once, a list means whenever those values change. Leave it out and it runs after every render.
try_it: Change the dependency array to [] and see what stops updating.

title: error.js catches broken pages
why_it_matters: One failed query shouldn't blank out the whole app.
explanation: An error file in a route folder catches errors thrown while rendering that route. It must be a client component. It receives the error and a reset function, which lets the user try again without reloading.
try_it: Throw an error in a page on purpose and see your error screen.

title: Store files in IndexedDB
why_it_matters: It can save Blobs, which localStorage can't.
explanation: IndexedDB handles structured data, including Blobs and Files. That makes it perfect for file viewers that remember recent documents or work offline. Writes go inside a transaction, and oncomplete tells you they finished.
try_it: Save a chosen file, reload, and read it back.

title: Why setTimeout 0 runs last
why_it_matters: Understanding the order of execution makes async code click.
explanation: JavaScript finishes the current code first. Callbacks from timers, events and promises wait in a queue until it is free. So even with a delay of 0, a timeout runs after all the synchronous lines.
try_it: Predict the output order, then run it.

title: Add an index to speed up reads
why_it_matters: Slow queries on big tables usually need one.
explanation: An index is like a book's index: the database jumps straight to matching rows instead of scanning the table. Index columns you filter or sort by often, like foreign keys. Too many indexes slow down writes, so don't add them blindly.
code:
create index bookings_created_at_idx
on bookings (created_at);
try_it: Think of two columns in your app that you filter by often.

title: Sticky header that actually sticks
why_it_matters: A header that disappears on scroll is annoying on long mobile pages.
explanation: position: sticky with a top value keeps an element visible once you scroll to it. Give it a background, or content will show through. If it fails, check the ancestors: overflow: hidden on a parent breaks it.
try_it: Add overflow: hidden to the parent and watch the header stop sticking.

title: Project idea: a booking system
why_it_matters: It combines SQL, auth and UI, which is exactly what teams build.
explanation: Build a small booking app: services, available time slots, and user bookings. The interesting bit is preventing double bookings with a database constraint. Add auth with Supabase and row-level security so users only see their bookings.
try_it: Sketch the tables you'd need: users, services, slots, bookings.

title: Mistake: sort() sorts text by default
why_it_matters: Numbers come back in a confusing order unless you add a comparator.
explanation: Without an argument, sort converts items to strings, so 10 comes before 9. Pass a compare function: a - b sorts ascending. Also remember sort changes the original array, so copy first if you need the old order.
try_it: Sort a list of prices from highest to lowest.

title: Make tap targets big enough
why_it_matters: Tiny buttons cause missed taps, especially for thumbs.
explanation: Aim for roughly 44 by 44 pixels for anything tappable, with space between neighbors. If the icon looks small, keep it small and grow the padding or min size instead. This helps everyone, not only people with motor difficulties.
try_it: Try tapping your smallest button with your thumb, one handed.

title: Stash: pause work in progress
why_it_matters: Switching branches with unfinished edits can be awkward.
explanation: git stash tucks away uncommitted changes and gives you a clean folder. Do what you need on another branch, then git stash pop to bring the work back. Commit small and often, so you need stash less.
code:
git stash
git switch other-branch
git stash pop
try_it: Stash a change, check git status, then pop it.

title: Debug AI code with console.log
why_it_matters: Printing what a value really is beats assuming.
explanation: Most bugs are wrong assumptions about data. Log the variable right before the failing line, including its type. Compare it with what the code expects. console.log is still the quickest way to see what's really happening.
try_it: Add two logs to the line that throws and read what they say.

title: Clean up your effects
why_it_matters: Forgotten timers and listeners pile up and cause memory leaks.
explanation: If an effect starts something ongoing, like an interval or an event listener, return a cleanup function. React calls it before running the effect again and when the component disappears. It keeps your app from doing work nobody sees.
try_it: Remove the cleanup and watch how many ticks you get after unmounting.

title: Show a 404 with notFound()
why_it_matters: Missing data deserves a proper not found page.
explanation: When a dynamic route can't find its record, call notFound() from next/navigation. Next.js renders the nearest not-found page and sends the right status code. It is cleaner than returning an empty page.
try_it: Visit an id that doesn't exist and check what the browser shows.

title: Copy to clipboard in one line
why_it_matters: Copy buttons are a tiny feature users love.
explanation: navigator.clipboard.writeText returns a promise. It requires a secure context, meaning https or localhost, and normally a user action like a click. Show feedback such as 'Copied', since the clipboard gives no visual cue.
try_it: Add a copy button next to a code block on a page you built.

title: Your first supabase-js select
why_it_matters: This is the bridge from SQL knowledge to app code.
explanation: supabase.from picks the table, select chooses columns like SQL's select, and order sorts. The call returns an object with data and error. Always handle both, because a failing query doesn't throw by itself.
code:
const { data, error } = await supabase
  .from("posts")
  .select("id, title")
  .order("created_at", { ascending: false });
try_it: Log data and error separately and break the table name on purpose.

title: Myth: z-index 9999 always wins
why_it_matters: Understanding stacking contexts ends the z-index guessing game.
explanation: z-index only works on positioned elements, flex items and grid items. Also, some properties like transform or opacity create a stacking context, trapping children inside. A child with z-index 9999 can't escape a parent that sits below another element.
code:
.modal { position: fixed; z-index: 10; }
.card  { position: relative; z-index: 1; }
try_it: Put transform: translateZ(0) on a parent and see if its child still overlaps the modal.

title: const doesn't freeze objects
why_it_matters: Sharing one object by accident changes it everywhere.
explanation: const stops you reassigning the variable, but the object inside can still change. Objects and arrays are passed by reference, so two variables can point to the same thing. Copy with spread when you need a separate one.
try_it: Do the same experiment with an array and push.

title: Mistake: input values are strings
why_it_matters: Form totals turn into '510' instead of 15 without this.
explanation: Everything read from an input is text. The plus sign joins text but adds numbers. Convert with Number() before doing math, and check for NaN if the user might type something odd.
try_it: Log Number('abc') and see what you get.

title: A smooth hover in two rules
why_it_matters: Small transitions make a UI feel polished without any JavaScript.
explanation: Put the transition on the normal state, not the hover state, so it plays both in and out. Name the property you animate rather than using all. On touch screens hover is unreliable, so never hide something important behind it.
code:
.btn { transition: transform 150ms ease; }
.btn:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); }
try_it: Add a transition to one button and try the same page on your phone.

title: Insert a row and check the error
why_it_matters: Silent failures are the worst kind.
explanation: insert takes an object whose keys match your column names. Supabase returns an error object instead of throwing, so check it every time. Row-level security problems and constraint failures show up there.
try_it: Insert a row with a column name that doesn't exist and read the message.

title: Fetch data with loading and error states
why_it_matters: Real users see loading and failure, not just the happy path.
explanation: Keep three pieces of state: the data, a loading flag and an error flag. Start loading as true. In finally, set loading to false. Show a different message for each state so the screen is never blank.
try_it: Add a visible error message for when the request fails.

title: Env vars: which ones reach the browser?
why_it_matters: This one rule decides whether a secret leaks.
explanation: Variables in .env.local are server-only by default. Only names starting with NEXT_PUBLIC_ are inlined into browser code. Never put a secret key behind that prefix, because anyone can read it in the page source.
code:
# .env.local
NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_NAME=DevTok
DATABASE_SECRET=keep-me-server-only
try_it: Log both variables in a client component and compare.

title: Native sharing with navigator.share
why_it_matters: On phones it opens the real share sheet, which feels app-like.
explanation: navigator.share lets a PWA share text or links through the device's own sharing menu. It works only on secure pages, after a user gesture, and not on every browser. Always check that it exists and keep a fallback like copy link.
try_it: Wire this into a button and test on your phone.

title: Announce updates with aria-live
why_it_matters: Toasts and form messages are silent to screen readers otherwise.
explanation: When text changes without a page load, a screen reader won't notice. An element with role status and aria-live polite announces its new text politely. The live region must exist in the page before its content changes.
try_it: Turn on a screen reader on your phone and trigger a message.

title: Push your project to GitHub
why_it_matters: It's your backup, your portfolio and your deploy source.
explanation: Create an empty repo on GitHub, then link it as origin. The -u flag on the first push remembers the branch, so later you can just type git push. Commit your work first, since push sends commits, not edits.
code:
git remote add origin git@github.com:YOUR-USERNAME/YOUR-REPO.git
git push -u origin main
try_it: Push a small project and open the repo page to check.

title: Test AI code with awkward inputs
why_it_matters: It works on the happy path and falls over on the real one.
explanation: Try an empty list, null, a very long string, a negative number, and a slow or failed network. AI tends to code for the example you gave it. Five awkward inputs find most of the bugs it left behind.
try_it: List five awkward inputs for your signup form and try each.

title: Why 0.1 + 0.2 isn't 0.3
why_it_matters: Money bugs start when you store prices as decimals.
explanation: Computers store decimals in binary, which can't represent some of them exactly. For money, store whole cents as integers, calculate with those, and divide by 100 only when displaying the result.
code:
console.log(0.1 + 0.2);   // 0.30000000000000004
const cents = 10 + 20;    // store integer cents
console.log(cents / 100); // 0.3
try_it: Store a price of 19.99 as 1999 and display it back correctly.

title: Animate transform, not left
why_it_matters: Animations that stutter on phones usually move the wrong property.
explanation: Animating left, top, width or height forces the browser to recalculate layout on every frame. transform and opacity can usually be handled much more cheaply. Use translate to move things, and scale to resize them.
try_it: Convert one animation in a project from left or top to transform: translate.

title: Project idea: an offline file tool
why_it_matters: It shows off browser APIs and respect for user privacy.
explanation: Build a client-side tool, like a text or image compressor or a document viewer, that works without uploading anything. Use the File API, make it a PWA and cache it for offline use. 'Your files never leave your device' is a strong pitch.
try_it: List the browser APIs your favorite tool would need.

title: Filter with eq and fetch one row
why_it_matters: Fetching one record by id is a daily task.
explanation: eq adds a where column = value filter. Chain more filters for more conditions. single returns one object instead of an array and gives an error if there isn't exactly one match. Perfect for a profile page.
code:
const { data, error } = await supabase
  .from("profiles")
  .select("*")
  .eq("id", userId)
  .single();
try_it: Call it with an id that doesn't exist and see the error.

title: What is a Promise, really?
why_it_matters: Every fetch and database call returns one.
explanation: A Promise is a placeholder for a value that arrives later. It is pending, then either fulfilled with a value or rejected with an error. You attach .then for success and .catch for failure, or use await.
try_it: Change the timeout to 2000 and watch when 'done' appears.

title: Mistake: the infinite render loop
why_it_matters: Your tab freezes, and the cause is two lines long.
explanation: Setting state inside an effect with no dependency array re-renders, which runs the effect, which sets state again. Add a dependency array, and only set state when something actually needs to change.
try_it: Add a console.log in an effect to see how often it runs.

title: Keep .env.local out of Git
why_it_matters: Leaked keys in a public repo get found and abused fast.
explanation: Your secrets file must never be committed. A fresh Next.js project usually ignores env files already, but checking takes five seconds. This command prints the rule that ignores the file. No output means it is not ignored.
code: git check-ignore -v .env.local
try_it: Run the command in your project folder right now.

title: Register your first service worker
why_it_matters: It is the engine behind offline PWAs.
explanation: A service worker is a script that sits between your page and the network. Registering it is just a feature check and one call. The file must be served from the scope it controls, so put sw.js at the site root. Requires https or localhost.
try_it: Look in DevTools, Application, Service Workers after registering.

title: Build a spinner with pure CSS
why_it_matters: Loading states show up in every app, so a tiny reusable one is useful.
explanation: A circle with one colored border side, rotated forever, makes a spinner. @keyframes defines what changes over time. The animation property names it, sets the duration, the timing and how often it repeats.
try_it: Make the spinner bigger and change its speed to 2 seconds.

title: async/await in plain English
why_it_matters: It makes asynchronous code read from top to bottom.
explanation: Mark a function async and you can use await inside it. await pauses that function until the promise settles, without freezing the page. It reads like normal step-by-step code, and it is how most modern fetch code is written.
try_it: Add a second await wait(1000) and a second log message.

title: Join tables in one supabase-js call
why_it_matters: You get nested data without writing SQL joins by hand.
explanation: If tables are linked by a foreign key, name the related table inside select. Supabase returns it as a nested array on each row. One round trip replaces several requests and loops.
try_it: Select a booking along with all its payments.

title: Run Lighthouse, fix the top item
why_it_matters: A score only helps if you act on it.
explanation: Lighthouse is built into Chrome DevTools and audits performance, accessibility, SEO and best practices. Run it in an incognito window, on mobile mode. Don't chase 100. Pick the one issue with the biggest impact and fix that first.
try_it: Run Lighthouse on your portfolio and fix one thing today.

title: Resolving a merge conflict calmly
why_it_matters: Conflicts look scary, but they're just a text-editing task.
explanation: Git marks the clashing lines with <<<<<<<, =======, and >>>>>>>. Edit the file to keep what you want, and delete all three markers. Then stage the file and commit. The app can't run until every marker is gone.
code:
git pull origin main
# conflict: edit the file, remove the markers
git add .
git commit -m "Resolve merge conflict"
try_it: Create a conflict deliberately in a test repo and resolve it.

title: Security red flags in AI code
why_it_matters: AI optimizes for 'it works', not 'it's safe'.
explanation: Watch for secret keys in client code, innerHTML or dangerouslySetInnerHTML with user input, tables without row-level security, and queries built from strings. If you see one, ask the AI to fix it and explain why it was risky.
try_it: Search your project for dangerouslySetInnerHTML and innerHTML.

title: Catch errors from await
why_it_matters: Networks fail, and your app shouldn't go blank when they do.
explanation: Wrap awaited code in try and catch. If any await rejects, execution jumps to catch, where you can show a message. Without it, the error becomes an unhandled rejection and the user sees nothing happen.
try_it: Turn off your network in DevTools and call load().

title: Respect people who hate motion
why_it_matters: Animations can cause real discomfort, and this is a one-time fix.
explanation: Some users turn on a reduce-motion setting because movement makes them dizzy. The prefers-reduced-motion media query lets you detect it. Wrap your animations in it, or switch them off for those users.
try_it: Turn on reduce motion in your OS settings and check that your site is calmer.

title: Don't store what you can compute
why_it_matters: Duplicate state drifts out of sync and creates bugs.
explanation: If a value can be calculated from existing state or props, calculate it during render. A total derived from the items list never gets out of date, because it is recomputed each time. Extra state means extra places to forget to update.
try_it: Find one piece of state in your code that is really derived.

title: Make an API route in 4 lines
why_it_matters: You get a backend endpoint with no extra server.
explanation: A route.js file inside the app folder defines an API endpoint. Export a function named after the HTTP method. Return a Response. The folder path becomes the URL, so app/api/hello/route.js serves /api/hello.
try_it: Open /api/hello in your browser and read the JSON.

title: Cache files for offline use
why_it_matters: This is the difference between a website and a PWA.
explanation: On install, the worker downloads and stores files in the Cache Storage. On every fetch, it answers from the cache first and falls back to the network. Bump the cache name when you ship new files, so old ones get replaced.
try_it: Turn on offline mode in DevTools and reload your page.

title: fetch in two steps
why_it_matters: Everyone gets stuck on why fetch needs two awaits.
explanation: The first await gives you the response once headers arrive. The second await, on res.json(), waits for the body to be read and parsed. Both steps return promises, so each needs its own await.
try_it: Log res.status before calling res.json().

title: Sign in with email and password
why_it_matters: Auth is built in, so you don't write password handling yourself.
explanation: signUp creates an account, and signInWithPassword logs in. Both return data and error. Supabase stores the session in the browser and refreshes it for you. Never store passwords yourself.
try_it: Create a test user from the Supabase dashboard and sign in as them.

title: Never remove the focus outline
why_it_matters: Keyboard users can't tell where they are on your page without it.
explanation: outline: none removes the ring that shows which element is focused. Instead of deleting it, restyle it. :focus-visible only shows the ring for keyboard navigation, so mouse users don't see it on clicks.
try_it: Press Tab on your site. Can you always see where the focus is?

title: Project idea: a tiny money ledger
why_it_matters: Fintech-style projects test care with data and edge cases.
explanation: Build an expense or wallet tracker. Store amounts as integer cents, format them with Intl, and never allow a negative balance without a rule. Add a transaction history and filters. Tests and clean data modelling will impress reviewers.
try_it: Write down three rules your ledger must never break.

title: Mistake: fetch doesn't throw on 404
why_it_matters: Your app may treat error pages as real data.
explanation: fetch only rejects for network failures. A 404 or 500 still resolves normally. Check res.ok, or the status code, and throw your own error when it is false. This single line prevents lots of confusing bugs.
try_it: Fetch a URL that doesn't exist and print res.ok.

title: Load heavy code only when needed
why_it_matters: A big library for a rarely used feature slows every visitor.
explanation: A dynamic import downloads code at the moment you use it, not at page load. Use it for charts, editors, PDF tools or anything behind a button. The first paint gets lighter, which matters on slow phone connections.
try_it: Find your biggest dependency and check whether you can lazy load it.

title: Every push to Vercel can get a preview
why_it_matters: You can test a branch online before it reaches production.
explanation: When Vercel is connected to your GitHub repo, pushes to the main branch update the live site. Pushes to other branches can get their own preview link. Check the preview on your phone before merging.
try_it: Push a branch and open its preview link on your phone.

title: Ask for two options and trade-offs
why_it_matters: The first answer isn't always the best fit.
explanation: Ask the AI for two different approaches and the pros and cons of each for your situation. You'll learn the design choices behind the code, and pick based on your project instead of whatever came first.
try_it: Ask for two ways to store a cart: localStorage or database.

title: Lift state up to share it
why_it_matters: Two sibling components can't talk directly in React.
explanation: When two components need the same data, move the state to their closest common parent and pass it down as props. The child receives a value and a function to change it. Data flows down, events flow up.
try_it: Sketch a small page with two components that share one value.

title: Accept data with a POST route
why_it_matters: Forms and fetch calls need somewhere to send data.
explanation: Export a POST function and read the body with await request.json(). Validate what you receive before using it, because anyone can call your endpoint. Return a status code that matches what happened, like 201 for created.
try_it: Call it with fetch and a JSON body from the browser console.

title: Make it installable with a manifest
why_it_matters: An install prompt turns your site into a home-screen app.
explanation: A manifest.json describes your app: name, short_name, start_url, display set to standalone, and a set of icons. Link it in the head, and add a theme-color. Together with a service worker, browsers can offer to install it.
code:
<link rel="manifest" href="/manifest.json">
<meta name="theme-color" content="#4f46e5">
try_it: Check DevTools, Application, Manifest for warnings on your site.

title: Who is signed in right now?
why_it_matters: Almost every protected feature starts with this check.
explanation: getUser asks Supabase's auth server who the current user is. It returns null when nobody is signed in. Prefer it over trusting stored session data when you make security decisions, because it verifies the token.
try_it: Show the user's email in your navbar when signed in.

title: Truncate long text with an ellipsis
why_it_matters: Long names and titles will break your layout if you don't plan for them.
explanation: Three rules together create a clean cut-off with three dots: no wrapping, hide the overflow, and set text-overflow. Inside flex items you also need min-width: 0, or the item refuses to shrink below its text.
try_it: Put a 60-character title inside a 200px card and apply these rules.

title: Run requests in parallel with Promise.all
why_it_matters: Waiting one by one makes screens load much slower than needed.
explanation: If two requests don't depend on each other, start both at once. Promise.all takes an array of promises and waits for all of them. You get the results in the same order. If any one fails, the whole thing rejects.
try_it: Time two sequential awaits against Promise.all using console.time.

title: Mistake: await inside forEach
why_it_matters: Your code says done while the work is still running.
explanation: forEach doesn't wait for async callbacks, so it starts them all and moves on. Use a for...of loop when you need to wait for each item in order. Use Promise.all with map when order doesn't matter.
try_it: Run it and notice which message appears first.

title: Container queries: components that adapt themselves
why_it_matters: Components stay reusable when they respond to their own space.
explanation: A media query asks about the screen. A container query asks about the parent. Mark a parent with container-type: inline-size, then use @container to style children based on its width. The same card can look right in a sidebar or main column.
try_it: Place one card component in a narrow and a wide parent and compare.

title: Myth: the anon key must be secret
why_it_matters: Knowing what is safe to expose stops both panic and real leaks.
explanation: The anon key is designed to live in browser code. What protects your data is row-level security, not hiding the key. With RLS enabled and no policies, the API returns no rows. Without RLS, anyone with the key can read the table.
code: alter table todos enable row level security;
try_it: Check in the dashboard that every table you made has RLS on.

title: useRef for things that aren't state
why_it_matters: It lets you touch the DOM or keep a value without re-rendering.
explanation: A ref holds a value in .current. Changing it does not cause a re-render. Attach one to an element to focus it, scroll it or measure it. It is an escape hatch, so reach for state first.
try_it: Auto-focus a search input when a component first mounts.

title: Set page titles with metadata
why_it_matters: Titles and descriptions decide how your site looks in search and shares.
explanation: Export a metadata object from a layout or page, and Next.js writes the head tags for you. Each page can override the layout's values. Write a different title for every page so tabs and search results make sense.
try_it: Give three pages three different titles and check the browser tabs.

title: Detect offline with two events
why_it_matters: Your app should say what's happening instead of failing silently.
explanation: The browser fires offline and online events on window. navigator.onLine gives the current state. Treat true as 'probably connected', not guaranteed. Use the events to show a banner and to queue work for later.
try_it: Toggle offline in DevTools and watch the events fire.

title: Debounce a search box
why_it_matters: Firing a request on every keystroke wastes data and flickers.
explanation: Debouncing waits until the user stops typing for a short moment before running your function. Each new keystroke cancels the previous timer. 300 milliseconds is a common starting point. It keeps API calls and rendering under control.
try_it: Wrap a search handler in debounce and watch the network tab.

title: Environment variables on Vercel
why_it_matters: 'Works locally, breaks online' is often a missing variable.
explanation: Your .env.local file stays on your machine. Add the same names and values in the Vercel project settings. Changes apply to new deployments, so redeploy after editing them. Names must match exactly, including NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefixes.
try_it: Compare your .env.local names with the ones in Vercel.

title: Commit before AI changes many files
why_it_matters: Git is your undo button when a change goes wrong.
explanation: Make a commit, or a branch, before letting AI touch several files. If the result breaks things, git restore or reset brings back your working version. Review changes with git diff before keeping them.
code:
git add -A
git commit -m "Checkpoint before AI refactor"
git switch -c ai-refactor
try_it: Make a checkpoint commit before your next AI-assisted change.

title: Grab elements with querySelector
why_it_matters: Everything in the DOM starts with finding the element.
explanation: querySelector takes a CSS selector and returns the first match, or null. querySelectorAll returns all matches as a list. Once you have an element, you can change its text, classes and attributes.
try_it: Change the text of any heading on a page from the console.

title: :has() — the parent selector arrived
why_it_matters: You can style a parent based on its children, without JavaScript.
explanation: The :has() selector matches an element if something inside it matches. Style a form field's wrapper when its input is invalid, or a card that contains a checked box. It replaces many small JS class toggles.
try_it: Highlight a label whenever its checkbox is checked using :has().

title: Explain your project in 60 seconds
why_it_matters: Interviewers always start with 'tell me about your project'.
explanation: Use three parts: the problem, what you built and how, and what you learned or would change. Mention one real decision, like picking Supabase, and why. Practice out loud so it sounds natural rather than memorized.
try_it: Record yourself explaining a project and listen back.

title: RLS policy: users see their own rows
why_it_matters: This single policy secures most beginner apps.
explanation: A select policy adds a hidden where clause for every query. auth.uid() returns the signed-in user's id. Comparing it to a user_id column means each person only ever sees their own rows, even if your frontend has bugs.
code:
create policy "read own todos"
on todos for select
to authenticated
using (auth.uid() = user_id);
try_it: Sign in as two users and confirm neither sees the other's rows.

title: Listen for a click
why_it_matters: Events are how a page responds to a person.
explanation: addEventListener takes an event name and a function. The browser calls your function when it happens and passes an event object with details. Keep the function small, and move bigger logic into named functions.
try_it: Log the event object by adding e as a parameter.

title: Write your first custom hook
why_it_matters: Hooks let you reuse logic, not just markup.
explanation: A custom hook is a function whose name starts with use and that calls other hooks. It bundles state and behavior so many components can share it. Each component using it still gets its own separate copy of the state.
try_it: Use useToggle to show and hide a menu in two different components.

title: Server Actions: forms without an API route
why_it_matters: You can run server code straight from a form.
explanation: Put 'use server' inside an async function and pass it to a form's action. On submit, the function runs on the server and receives the FormData. It keeps secrets safe and removes a lot of fetch boilerplate.
try_it: Submit the form and find the log in your terminal.

title: IntersectionObserver: know what's on screen
why_it_matters: It beats scroll listeners for lazy loading and animations.
explanation: IntersectionObserver calls you when an element enters or leaves the viewport. No scroll events, no manual math. Use it to load content when it nears the screen, trigger animations once, or build infinite scroll.
try_it: Fade in each section once as it scrolls into view.

title: Swipeable carousel, no JavaScript
why_it_matters: Horizontal swiping is native on phones, so use it.
explanation: Make a flex row that scrolls horizontally, then add scroll-snap. The container snaps items into place, and each child declares where it aligns. Children at about 80% width let the next one peek out, hinting there is more.
try_it: Build a row of five cards and swipe it on your phone.

title: Event delegation for lists
why_it_matters: One listener beats a hundred, and works on items added later.
explanation: Events bubble up from the clicked element through its parents. Attach one listener to the list, then use e.target.closest to find which item was clicked. New items work automatically without any extra wiring.
try_it: Add an li with JavaScript and check that clicking it still works.

title: RLS insert needs WITH CHECK
why_it_matters: Without it, users can create rows that belong to someone else.
explanation: using filters rows that exist. with check validates rows being written. An insert policy needs with check, otherwise a user could insert rows with another person's user_id. Match it to auth.uid() to stop that.
code:
create policy "insert own todos"
on todos for insert
to authenticated
with check (auth.uid() = user_id);
try_it: Try inserting a row with someone else's user_id and read the error.

title: defer: stop scripts blocking the page
why_it_matters: Render-blocking scripts delay what your visitors can see.
explanation: A normal script in the head pauses HTML parsing while it downloads and runs. The defer attribute downloads it in the background and runs it after the page is parsed, in order. It's the simplest speed win for plain HTML.
code:
<!-- blocks rendering -->
