<script src="app.js"></script>

<!-- doesn't block -->
<script src="app.js" defer></script>
try_it: Add defer to a script in a project and check it still works.

title: NEXT_PUBLIC_ values are baked in at build
why_it_matters: Changing one in Vercel does nothing until you redeploy.
explanation: Next.js replaces NEXT_PUBLIC_ variables with their real values while building. The browser code contains the final text, not a lookup. So after changing one, trigger a new build. Server-only variables are read at runtime on the server.
try_it: Change a public variable, redeploy, and confirm the new value appears.

title: Quiz yourself on the code you shipped
why_it_matters: Understanding beats a working app you can't explain.
explanation: After each feature, ask the AI to write five questions about the code it gave you, then answer them without looking. Wrong answers show exactly what to study next. Over time, you'll need the AI less for basics.
try_it: Generate five questions about your last feature, answer them cold.

title: Stop the form from reloading the page
why_it_matters: Forms refresh the page by default, wiping your JavaScript state.
explanation: Submitting a form navigates by default. Call e.preventDefault() in the submit handler to stop that. Then read the values with FormData, using the name attribute of each input.
try_it: Make sure your input has a name attribute, or get() returns null.

title: Bottom nav that avoids the home bar
why_it_matters: Fixed bottom bars on modern phones collide with the gesture area.
explanation: Add viewport-fit=cover to your viewport meta tag, then pad fixed bottom elements with env(safe-area-inset-bottom). It is zero on devices without a notch or gesture bar, so it is safe everywhere. Great for PWAs and app-style layouts.
try_it: Add viewport-fit=cover to your meta tag and test a bottom bar on a modern phone.

title: Mistake: onClick={save()}
why_it_matters: The function runs during render, not on click.
explanation: Parentheses call a function immediately. onClick needs the function itself, not its result. Pass the name, or wrap a call in an arrow function when you need to pass arguments.
code:
<button onClick={save()}>Save</button>      {/* runs on render */}
<button onClick={save}>Save</button>        {/* runs on click */}
<button onClick={() => remove(id)}>Delete</button>
try_it: Search your code for onClick={ followed by a function name with parentheses.

title: Read query strings with searchParams
why_it_matters: Search pages and filters live in the URL, so they can be shared.
explanation: Server pages receive searchParams as a prop, holding the part after the question mark. Awaiting it is safe in all versions. Using the URL for state means refresh, back and share links all keep working.
try_it: Visit /?q=sql and read the output.

title: Read and build URLs with URLSearchParams
why_it_matters: Filters and pagination are easier to share when they live in the URL.
explanation: URLSearchParams parses the query string for you. get reads a value, set changes it, and toString builds the new text with proper escaping. It's much safer than slicing strings by hand.
try_it: Build a link with a search term that contains a space and an ampersand.

title: textContent vs innerHTML: a security gap
why_it_matters: innerHTML with user input lets attackers run code on your page.
explanation: innerHTML parses a string as HTML, so a comment containing markup can run scripts through event attributes. textContent treats everything as plain text. Use it by default, and only use innerHTML for content you fully control.
try_it: Search your code for innerHTML and check where each value comes from.

title: Upload a file to Storage
why_it_matters: File uploads power avatars, documents and your own client-side tools.
explanation: Pick a bucket with storage.from, then upload a path and a File object. Prefixing the path with the user's id keeps files organised and makes storage policies easy to write. Check error before assuming it worked.
try_it: Create a private bucket and upload one file from the dashboard first.

title: Why your absolute element flew away
why_it_matters: It explains every 'my badge is in the wrong corner' moment.
explanation: An absolutely positioned element is placed relative to its nearest positioned ancestor. If none exists, it uses the whole page. Give the parent position: relative and the child's top and right values start making sense.
try_it: Remove position: relative from .card and see where the badge goes.

title: 'I don't know yet' is an okay answer
why_it_matters: How you handle gaps matters more than pretending.
explanation: If you're asked something you can't answer, say so, then show how you'd find out: check the docs, test a small example, read the error. Teams hire people who learn well. Bluffing is easy to spot and costs trust.
try_it: Practice finishing the sentence: 'I'm not sure, but here's how I'd find out...'

title: JSON: the text format of the web
why_it_matters: Every API and localStorage conversation uses it.
explanation: JSON is text that looks like a JavaScript object. JSON.stringify turns a value into text so you can send or store it. JSON.parse turns text back into a value. Functions and undefined don't survive the trip.
try_it: Stringify an object containing a function and see what disappears.

title: Measure before you optimize
why_it_matters: Guessing what's slow wastes time on the wrong things.
explanation: console.time and console.timeEnd give you a quick stopwatch around any code. For whole pages, use the DevTools Performance tab. Fix the thing the numbers point at, then measure again to confirm it really improved.
try_it: Time a function in your own project and write down the result.

title: Build locally before you push
why_it_matters: It catches errors that dev mode forgives.
explanation: npm run dev is forgiving. npm run build is what Vercel runs, and it fails on things like type errors and missing imports. Also, Linux servers treat Button.js and button.js as different files, even if your computer doesn't.
code:
npm run build
npm run start
try_it: Run a production build of your latest project and fix what appears.

title: Check that an npm package really exists
why_it_matters: Invented package names can lead you to install something malicious.
explanation: AI sometimes suggests packages that don't exist, and attackers sometimes publish fakes with those names. Before npm install, check the name on the registry, its publisher, and that others actually use it. This one command shows details.
code: npm view react name version
try_it: Check one dependency in your project: who publishes it?

title: Pass functions as props
why_it_matters: It's how a child component tells its parent something happened.
explanation: Props can be functions too. The parent passes a callback, and the child calls it with data when something happens, like a click. Name them onSomething so their purpose is obvious. Data flows down as props, events flow up through callbacks.
try_it: Add an onDelete prop to a list item and log which id was clicked.

title: Fix 'window is not defined'
why_it_matters: It is the most common Next.js error for people using browser APIs.
explanation: Server code has no window, document or localStorage, and components are first rendered on the server. Read browser values inside useEffect, which only runs in the browser. Store them in state so the page can update.
try_it: Move a localStorage read from the top of a component into useEffect.

title: Format money with Intl.NumberFormat
why_it_matters: Fintech-style screens need correct currency formatting.
explanation: Intl.NumberFormat formats numbers for a locale and currency, adding separators and symbols correctly. Keep amounts as integer cents in your data and divide by 100 only when formatting. Never build currency strings by hand.
try_it: Switch the locale and currency and compare outputs.

title: Private files need signed URLs
why_it_matters: Public links to private documents are a serious leak.
explanation: A public bucket serves files to anyone with the link. For sensitive files keep the bucket private and create a signed URL that expires. The second argument is how many seconds the link stays valid.
try_it: Generate a 60-second link and test that it stops working after.

title: Why your CSS is being ignored
why_it_matters: Specificity explains most 'my style does nothing' bugs.
explanation: When two rules clash, the more specific selector wins, not the later one. An id beats a class, which beats an element. Fix it with a better selector, not !important. Check DevTools: the crossed-out rule lost the fight.
try_it: Inspect an element in DevTools and find a crossed-out rule. Why did it lose?

title: Split your code with import and export
why_it_matters: One giant file becomes unreadable fast.
explanation: A module is a file that exports things and imports what it needs. Named exports are imported with curly braces and must match the name. A default export can be imported under any name. Modules keep your code organised.
try_it: Move one helper function from your main file into its own file.
